segments.title: Chương 209: 0209【Lâm Đại Ngọc nhập trạch】
segments.content:
Chapter 212 0209 Lin Daiyu Joins

In Report Hall 202 of the Guanghua School, not only were the seats full, but the aisles were also completely packed with people standing.

No tickets were needed; anyone who came could listen.

Between the entrance and the lecture stage, there was a host's table, where a few student council members from the Guanghua School were standing.

Chen Guiliang carried the gifts from the entrepreneur students over and shoved them under the host's table.

"What's this?" asked Song Yu, a student council member and tonight's host.

Chen Guiliang said, "The students from the Guanghua advanced studies program heard Chen Xiaoxu was at Peking University and asked me to bring her some gifts."

"Oh." Song Yu didn't ask any more questions.

Chen Guiliang took the opportunity to stand there and didn't move.

He had arrived late and couldn't get a seat, and he couldn't be bothered to squeeze into the aisle with others, so he simply stood behind the host's table, huddling with the student council members.

He didn't act like an outsider at all.

A student council member named Zhang Jun said, "CEO Chen, you might as well just transfer to our Guanghua School."

"I've been thinking about it," Chen Guiliang replied perfunctorily.

Students in the Yuanpei Program could choose their major in the second semester of their sophomore year.

If Chen Guiliang chose management as his major now, all his academic and scholarly activities would be transferred to the Guanghua School. He would be considered a member of the Guanghua School. At the same time, his student status and administrative affiliation would remain with the Yuanpei Program.

It was like having a dual identity.

Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered to choose a major. He liked his current status as a free agent.

There were many other Yuanpei Program students like him; a few exceptional ones didn't even start choosing a major until their senior year.

Chen Guiliang chatted idly with the student council members, then took a call from Tao Chenggang. He hung up when he saw Chen Xiaoxu arrive.

Some students had already gone up to ask for autographs, but most people were still quite reserved.

After signing twenty or thirty autographs, she finally managed to deal with the star-struck students. Chen Xiaoxu walked over to the host's table to talk with the student council member, Song Yu. Song Yu, through some unknown means, had managed to persuade Chen Xiaoxu to come after much persistence.

This Song Yu was quite handsome, dressed in a suit and tie, with a haircut even shorter than Li Yuchun's. At a glance, one might mistake her for a very handsome man.

Only when she spoke did you realize she was a woman.

"Ms. Chen, hello," Chen Guiliang said, pulling several gifts out from under the table. "Peking University has an entrepreneur advanced studies program. When the students heard you were coming, they asked me to bring you some gifts to express their admiration. They're not expensive things; one person even just sent a postcard."

Chen Xiaoxu thought Chen Guiliang was also part of the student council and said with a smile, "Please convey my thanks to them as well."

She looked well; there was no sign of illness.

But next month, she would be diagnosed with stage two breast cancer. This was a relatively early stage, and with the medical technology of 2006, the five-year survival rate was around 80 percent.

The cure rate was quite high.

Provided one was willing to cooperate with the treatment.

Chen Guiliang handed her a business card, a Class-A card with his personal phone number.

Chen Xiaoxu took it and glanced at it: Founder & CEO of ByteDance, Founder & CEO of Game Science.

At that moment, Song Yu had already walked onto the lecture stage and started introducing the topic of today's speech.

Chen Xiaoxu asked curiously, "You're not a student?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm a student too."

"Starting a business is very difficult. I wish you success." Chen Xiaoxu didn't seem to follow the news much; she hadn't even been managing her own company for the past two years.

Chen Guiliang didn't explain further. Instead, he seized the opportunity and said, "My company is right outside the east gate of Peking University. If possible, I'd very much like to invite Ms. Chen for a visit, to talk to everyone about entrepreneurship."

Chen Xiaoxu politely declined, "I have other things to do tomorrow."

"Even just a few minutes would be fine. The team would be thrilled," Chen Guiliang said.

Chen Xiaoxu was staying at Changchun Xinyuan tonight, which was very close to the east gate of Peking University. She thought for a moment and said, "Alright, I'll come for 30 minutes. I have other things to do in the morning."

She felt she could offer some encouragement to the student entrepreneurs.

Starting a business was quite difficult.

On the lecture stage, Song Yu led from dreams to entrepreneurship, then from Li Ning to Chen Xiaoxu, before giving a detailed introduction of Chen Xiaoxu herself and her company.

After about six and a half minutes of rambling, she finally invited Chen Xiaoxu to the stage to speak.

Song Yu returned to the host's table. "What were you guys talking about just now?"

"I invited her to speak at my company for a bit tomorrow," Chen Guiliang said.

"She agreed?"

"Yeah."

"Wow, you're the impressive one. It took me half a year of pestering to get her to agree to speak at Peking University."

"You're more impressive for managing to invite her at all."

Standing on the lecture stage, Chen Xiaoxu was visibly nervous.

Just as she was about to speak, she clutched her chest and exhaled. After several failed attempts to start, she made the students in the audience laugh. She clutched her chest and laughed along with them.

Her expression and gestures were like those of a young girl who had not yet stepped out into society.

She smiled, tucked her hair back, patted her chest, and said with a breath, "I really wish Ms. Song could have kept talking, so I wouldn't have to come on stage and could have remained in the audience. Because for many years, I've rarely attended lectures with so many people. And, I rarely accept media interviews, because I always feel I haven't studied enough…"

Chen Xiaoxu began to talk about her life experiences. Chen Guiliang found it quite interesting, mainly because there were some things he had never heard before.

For instance, Chen Xiaoxu said that when she wanted to travel abroad, the Americans denied her visa several times because they suspected she had an inclination to immigrate.

After finally managing to travel to the U.S. via Germany, a friend urged her to just stay in America. Chen Xiaoxu said the reason she didn't stay was that she couldn't bring herself to wash dishes for a living; she felt her friend had a very tiring job in the U.S.

In the end, she spent all her money and returned to China.

She said she had saved up 30,000 yuan at the time. A businessman had tricked her into buying 20,000 yuan worth of stocks, and she used the remaining 10,000 for her travel expenses to America. By the time she returned to China, those stocks had already risen from 1 yuan to 7 yuan per share.

These stocks became the capital for her to start her own company.

Next was her entrepreneurial experience. She didn't preach any grand principles, only talked about the people and things she had encountered.

She spoke with wit and humor, not at all like a pessimistic and negative person.

"This character, 'Ren' (benevolence). On the left is the radical for 'person,' and on the right are two horizontal strokes… If we understand the character 'Ren,' we will know how to be a proper person. The 'person' on the left represents a life, and the two strokes on the right encompass oneself and others."

"All life is composed of me and him. Sometimes, the top stroke represents yourself, a father, and the bottom stroke might be your son. Other times, you are a husband, and the bottom stroke is your wife…"

"Benevolence means having others in your heart… If you are a doctor and you don't have others in your heart, you might prescribe a high-priced medicine for a patient just for a kickback, instead of thinking first about saving lives… As people in the media industry, it is especially important to have benevolence in our hearts, to bear social responsibility, because we influence the entire society…"

"If the whole of society is misled by our ideas and develops an unhealthy trend or direction, we are actually destroying the world… We must not produce any works that contain erroneous ideas that mislead the public, nor anything that does not conform to traditional Chinese morals…"

After the applause, it was time for audience questions.

The first person to get the microphone was, surprisingly, a student from the entrepreneur advanced studies program. Who knows how he managed to sneak in.

The moment he opened his mouth, it was a stream of flattery. He even said he had chased his idol all the way here, and his words became more and more mushy. "I'd like to ask my Sister Lin a question…"

"Hahaha!"

The whole hall burst into laughter.

"After becoming a household name overnight, why did you choose to change careers and do other things?"

Chen Xiaoxu said, "Everything I've done was not meticulously planned, but the result of a series of accidents… I'm a rational person, not suited to be an actress… When I played Lin Daiyu crying, my mind was actually on other things. I wasn't emotionally invested at all…"

Chen Guiliang thought to himself, no matter how rational a person is, they can still be haunted by the shadow of a role. Otherwise, she wouldn't have given up on treatment.

The next day.

Chen Xiaoxu asked for directions and arrived at the Peking University Science Park Building.

She had come to Beijing alone this time, without even an assistant by her side.

As she walked towards the elevator, Chen Guiliang, who had been playing on his phone in the lobby, quickly walked over and said, "Good morning, Ms. Chen."

"Not that early. I overslept," Chen Xiaoxu said.

Chen Guiliang said, "There's a cafeteria right here. Would you like to have breakfast first?"

"I've already eaten," Chen Xiaoxu said.

The morning rush hour for work was over, and the elevator was empty.

As they rode the elevator up, Chen Xiaoxu asked, "How old are you?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I'll be 20 in three months."

"You're quite young, starting a company at this age." Given her age, if she had married and had children early, her son would have been as old as Chen Guiliang.

She was treating Chen Guiliang completely as a junior.

After exiting the elevator, she followed Chen Guiliang to the company. The moment she walked in, she realized she had been "tricked."

ByteDance was even larger than her own company!

What tough start for a university student entrepreneur?

*Clap clap clap clap!*

The employees stood up one by one and applauded.

The woman before them was a frequent guest on summer television, her appearance rate only slightly lower than that of Sun Wukong and the White Snake.

Chen Guiliang led her on a tour of the company's various departments, explaining in detail, "I started the company in my freshman year with my manuscript fees. Last year, I received a round of venture capital… Our company's products include…"

"You're a writer too?" Chen Xiaoxu asked curiously.

Secretary Hu Yuexia presented the first three volumes of *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*. Chen Guiliang took them and handed them to Chen Xiaoxu. "My humble work. I hope Ms. Chen will grace it with her critique."

"You wrote this? A friend recommended this book to me!" Chen Xiaoxu was quite surprised.

This brought them closer. It was no longer a pure exchange between entrepreneurs, but a conversation between a literature lover and a writer.

Chen Guiliang led her to a computer, briefly introduced Xiaonei, and then gave a detailed introduction of Kaixin. "On this website, you can interact with many new friends. You can upload your photos, or write some articles. It could be a book review, or just a random record of your mood…"

Chen Guiliang specifically opened the homepages of several cultural celebrities to entice Chen Xiaoxu to register an account.

As expected, Chen Xiaoxu became interested. She even sat down at the computer and browsed through the articles by those cultural figures. She carefully read Li Ao's articles several times.

Chen Guiliang thought: With more and more celebrities and entrepreneurs being invited, the name "Kaixin" is a bit lame. Maybe I should change it to "Hainei" ahead of schedule.

A bosom friend afar brings a distant land near.

Besides, one could tell from the name that it was a sister site to Xiaonei.

He couldn't change it all at once. He could first change it to "Kaixin Hainei," then after a while, to "Hainei Kaixin." Finally, he could drop the "Kaixin" part.

"How do I register an account?" Chen Xiaoxu asked.

Chen Guiliang pointed at the computer screen. "Click here… If celebrities want to be verified, they must link their mobile number… The personal homepage can be customized, and there's also an 'electronic den,' a feature we launched last year. In the electronic den, you can furnish it with furniture, appliances, pets, and even invite friends over for a visit…"

Chen Xiaoxu definitely had the heart of a young girl. She completely forgot she had other things to do that morning and forgot to pay attention to the cultural celebrities. All her attention was now on decorating her electronic den.

"I have to top up to buy this electronic sofa?"

"I'll activate it for you right away."

"No, no, I'll top up myself."

Chen Guiliang added, "There are other mini-games. This is 'Happy Farm,' where you can grow and steal vegetables. This is 'Parking Wars,' with all sorts of luxury cars… And there's 'Happy Shop,' where you can run your own store…"

After learning about all the features, Chen Xiaoxu remarked with emotion, "This is a completely different world on the internet. You can have another life without ever leaving your home!"

Perhaps, if she became a "gaming addict," she would feel a little more attached to this world.

"You can also activate mobile Weibo. Your followers can receive updates via text message…"

After getting Chen Xiaoxu's consent, Chen Guiliang took a photo with her on his phone and then posted it on Weibo: "Honored to have invited Teacher Chen Xiaoxu to join Kaixin today."

Chen Xiaoxu had a huge number of fans.

A large portion of the entrepreneurs in China were, to some extent, her fans.

By getting Chen Xiaoxu to join Kaixin, it was likely that many entrepreneurs would come and register accounts on their own!

(End of this chapter)
